text:
The part that sets a watch's pace was redesigned by one British watchmaker.

For about 250 years most watches used one escapement design that needs oil. In the 1970s George Daniels designed the co-axial escapement, with parts that roll instead of slide. Omega launched it in April 1999.

Which one would you rather have, a watch that needs oil or one that needs less? Tell us below.

Source: OMEGA chronicle, '1999: a revolutionary new escapement' (launch date 12 April 1999, read 28 November 2026); Worn & Wound, 'The co-axial escapement: an horological hit' (invention in the 1970s, one source says 1974).
